strategy_objective_guidance:
- Single scored quantity: `combined_score = (dmin/dmax)^2 / (1/4.165849767)`. No other terms; runtime is reported but not scored (only the implicit timeout). Score is uncapped, so beating the reference (score > 1) is possible and is the only lever.
- Hard constraints: return a finite NumPy array of exactly shape (14, 3); dmax > 0. Any exception → score 0, so robustness (always returning a valid incumbent) is essential but not itself scored.
- The objective is scale/translation/rotation invariant — only the *ratio* matters. Equivalently: maximize t s.t. d(i,j)² ≥ t and d(i,j)² ≤ 1 for all pairs — a smooth constrained NLP with 91 pairwise constraints in 42 variables.
- No conflicting weighted terms; the only tradeoff is dmin up vs dmax down, both captured in one ratio. The largest remaining lever is purely geometric: finding a better 14-point packing (best-known squared ratio slightly above 1/4.1658 ≈ 0.24).
- The program receives no input at all — it must *construct* the point set offline. Full batch/offline global optimization is permitted; no streaming/causality concerns. Precomputation inside the function is fine within the timeout.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- Symmetric polyhedral constructions: build candidates from icosahedral/dodecahedral symmetry groups, e.g., vertices of the icosahedron plus face/edge centers, or two rotated rings; scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation for generating symmetric orbits; score each with scipy.spatial.distance.pdist. These give strong deterministic incumbents.

strategies.title: [charge-relaxation-anneal] Force-directed Thomson-style relaxation with annealed
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: charge-relaxation-anneal
Replacement scope: Replace the seed-generation phase inside `min_max_dist_dim3_14()` (the `for k in (4,5,6,7)` ring-grid block and its L-BFGS-B ring solves) with a physics-style relaxation pipeline; keep `_polish`, `_epigraph_solve`, `_kkt_refine`, `_consider`, and the fallback untouched.
Compute budget: 12 deterministic starts (RandomState(3), points uniform on unit sphere plus one seeded start from the current incumbent's convex-hull vertices reprojected), each ≤ 1500 relaxation iterations of O(n²) vectorized force steps (~2 s total), then only the top 3 relaxates go through the existing `_polish` + `_kkt_refine`. Expected evaluation time ≤ current 46 s.
Gain mechanism: The ring families constrain all points to two coplanar orbits, so the incumbent's contact graph is a ring-adjacency graph. A pairwise-repulsion relaxation (each pair pushed apart along its connecting vector with force ∝ 1/d², plus a soft penalty pulling the diameter toward 1, annealed from loose to tight) lets the contact graph reorganize into arbitrary triangulated topologies — e.g. fullerene-like or deltahedral graphs — that no two-ring parametrization can express. This is a genuinely new degree of freedom: the *topology* of the near-contact graph, not just its parameters. After relaxation each candidate is normalized (dmax=1) and fed to the existing guarded epigraph/KKT polish, so acceptance stays monotone in the exact squared ratio and the (14,3) finite-shape constraint is preserved by `_consider` plus the final fallback.
Plan: (1) For each start, place 14 points on the unit sphere (seeded), set dmax=1 by normalization. (2) Iterate: compute pairwise unit vectors; move each point by step size η·Σ_{j≠i} (x_i−x_j)/|d_ij|³ (repulsion) minus λ·Σ over the current dmax-attaining pairs of (x_i−x_j)/dmax (diameter contraction), with η annealed 0.02→0.001 and λ annealed 0→0.5 over the schedule; renormalize dmax=1 each iteration. (3) Score with `_ratio`, keep top 3, run `_polish(P, soft_iters=200, rounds=4)` then `_kkt_refine` on each, all through `_consider`. The incumbent fallback and every guard remain, so hard validity is never at risk.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the full 42-dimensional contact topology (relaxation can reach non-ring, non-icosahedral deltahedral graphs); the incumbent is provably confined to two-ring orbits, so if any 14-point configuration with squared ratio > 0.2400509 has a non-two-ring contact graph, this strategy can reach it — falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 1.000016 on the evaluator.

strategies.title: [helical-zigzag-orbit] Two-start Boerdijk–Coxeter helix construction with free t
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: metropolis-basin-hopping
Replacement scope: Replace the discrete contact-graph swap walk block (the `if bestP is not None:` walk with `_active`/`_move` and its 40 steps) with a Metropolis basin-hopping loop; keep everything else (ring seeds, `_polish`, epigraph, KKT, `_consider`, fallback) unchanged.
Compute budget: ≤ 60 hop iterations; each hop = Gaussian perturbation (σ annealed 0.08→0.01) + short `_polish(soft_iters=100, rounds=2, maxiter=250)`; temperature annealed linearly; ~15 s, replacing the ~15 s the swap walk already costs, so total time stays ≈ 46 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's walk only accepts candidates that improve or tie the incumbent and generates moves along existing active-edge directions — it is a monotone hill climber that provably cannot cross any barrier where all short-polished perturbations score strictly below the incumbent. Metropolis acceptance at temperature T (accept a worse candidate with probability exp(−Δr/T) on the squared-ratio scale) lets the *walking* configuration descend and re-ascend into a different basin, while the scored incumbent is still updated only through `_consider` (strict improvement), so the returned result is monotone-safe. This is a new escape mechanism (non-monotone exploration), not a new seed family.
Plan: Pcur = bestP; for step in 60: Q = Pcur + σ·RandomState(101+step).randn(14,3); Qp = _polish(Q, short settings); Δ = _ratio(Qp) − _ratio(Pcur); accept if Δ ≥ 0 or rand < exp(Δ/T_step); always `_consider(Qp)`; anneal σ and T. Final `_kkt_refine` on the incumbent as before. Hard constraints preserved: every candidate is finite-checked, `_consider` only stores valid (14,3) arrays, and the existing fallback covers total failure.
Expected-gain check: the new mechanism is non-monotone basin traversal (accepting strictly worse intermediates), which the incumbent's tie-or-improve walk cannot perform by construction; falsifiable threshold: combined_score > 1.000016, i.e. discovery of any basin with squared ratio above 0.2400509.
